Its stationarity infinity norm was 2.131551974043997e-10 N·m, complementarity residual was 6.689144995757621e-16 N·m, and primal violation was 5.551115123125783e-17 m. The minimum slack margin was -5.551115123125783e-17 m and native soft-length excess was 5.551115123125783e-17 m; these tiny strict violations are retained even though the recorded tolerance-based qualification passed. All three tendons were active with positive equilibrium tensions, with maximum tension 1.7214417663040709 N; minimum reduced stiffness was 0.0920759180326094 N·m/rad. The initial preflight found zero native-enabled contacts and each tendon at a unilateral payout boundary, with path length 0.2540000000000002 m, payout 0.2540000000000001 m, and signed residual 1.1102230246251565e-16 m. input.expected_observation: Across distinct proposals, both tendon counts 3 and 4 and multiple Young's-modulus values are exercised; at least one qualified proposal has lower aggregate static task violation over s3_positive and s3_negative than the search's initial point, with the best proposal retaining contact-free, capacity-respecting passive equilibrium.
input.fixed_conditions: Keep the frozen Base-only passive task, unilateral fixed-payout semantics, no active control, passive-equilibrium model, mount, permitted family generator, solver, and all unselected coordinates fixed by the fresh family-default search center. Hold segment count at 2 and whole-chain span strategy fixed. Do not perform finite-time integration, the full ten-condition task, physical Replay, BDF, NMPC, or RL. The finite Young's-modulus interval is 2000000 to 5000000 Pa, and the only discrete alternatives are tendon counts 3 and 4.
input.hypothesis: Because candidate_19 established that a three-tendon fixed-payout assembly can sustain a qualified, contact-free unloaded equilibrium with all tendons positively active, a small mixed search that changes tendon count and backbone Young's modulus can reveal whether extra unilateral routing coverage and finite stiffness variation reduce the registered static localization violations under opposite near-base transverse loads without losing passive-equilibrium qualification.
input.interpretation: The initial diagnostic supports a locally stable, fully engaged three-tendon baseline mechanism but provides no design direction or task acceptance. This bounded search is worthwhile because tendon count tests a discrete change in unilateral directional coverage while Young's modulus tests a continuous stiffness tradeoff, and three evaluations can provide an initial interaction check. Segment count, span strategy, routing geometry, payout, lengths, and sections remain fixed to avoid confounding within the small allowance; they remain open in the full FamilySpace. Static task violation is only a diagnostic proxy, so even the best mathematical candidate will not establish eight-second, ten-condition, dynamic, or independent task acceptance.
input.stopping_condition: Stop after at most 6 distinct generated proposals and at most 3 passive-equilibrium mathematical evaluations, or earlier if admission or generation prevents legal mixed-coordinate evaluation. The request must include both s3_positive and s3_negative for at least one evaluated structure and should exercise both tendon counts and more than one Young's-modulus value within the allowance.
input.weakening_observation: The search fails to exercise both coordinates, all evaluated proposals fail equilibrium qualification, or qualified proposals show no reduction in static task violation across the tested tendon-count and modulus changes. Such an outcome would weaken this specific mixed-coordinate mechanism hypothesis but would not exclude unsearched routing, section, span, payout, length, or broader material designs.

plan.expected_observation: A non-dynamic structural diagnostic should show that transverse loading near an interior material coordinate activates at least one tendon and produces a nonuniform deformation or stiffness pattern, rather than rigidly translating the tip with the loaded point.
plan.fixed_conditions: Use the frozen passive task, fixed-base starts, unilateral tendons, fixed payout semantics with omitted payouts equal to actual zero-state route lengths, inherited prototypes and default discretization; no active control, dynamics, contact, or task acceptance claim.
plan.hypothesis: A two-segment base-only passive backbone with three equally spaced unilateral tendons routed from the fixed base across both segments can develop direction-dependent geometric tension under transverse loading, allowing appreciable interior x displacement while suppressing distal-tip and out-of-plane displacement without active control.
plan.interpretation: This deliberately small symmetric candidate is a neutral mechanism probe, not a claimed winner. Three tendons are the smallest circumferential set that can reveal load-direction engagement while retaining a compact topology. Geometry and material defaults remain fixed to avoid confounding the first diagnostic.
plan.stopping_condition: Stop this initial construction after one fresh legal candidate is registered; then choose exactly one cheap non-dynamic mathematical diagnostic before considering any search.
plan.weakening_observation: The diagnostic shows no unilateral tendon engagement, nearly uniform point-to-tip motion, excessive out-of-plane coupling, singularity, or no mechanism for localizing deformation.

decision.selected_method: unloaded qualification inspect of unilateral tendon active set and payout consistency
selected_variables: tendon geometric length minus fixed payout

plan.expected_observation: The unloaded qualification converges without prohibited contact, reports payout-consistent tendon lengths, and identifies at least one taut tendon while retaining a nonsingular equilibrium.
plan.fixed_conditions: Keep candidate_19 geometry, material properties, mount, three unilateral tendons, pretensions, force limits, fixed payout semantics, frozen unloaded solver and multistart, and the native task scene unchanged. Perform no loading episode and no finite-time integration.
plan.hypothesis: At the frozen unloaded re-equilibrated state, candidate_19 has a qualified non-contact equilibrium in which at least one unilateral tendon is taut under the fixed payout semantics, providing a mechanically engaged pathway that could later redistribute transverse load rather than behaving as a tendon-free backbone.
plan.interpretation: This is a cheap mechanism prerequisite test, not evidence of full ten-condition task performance. A qualified taut tendon supports proceeding to Reporter-assisted consideration of bounded mixed search; failure or universal slackness argues against spending the remaining three mathematical evaluations on routing/topology search.
plan.stopping_condition: Stop this diagnostic after the single registered unloaded qualification inspection and send the saved result to the existing Reporter before making another scientific Plan.
plan.weakening_observation: Qualification fails, prohibited initial contact is present, every tendon is slack or geometrically inconsistent with payout, or the equilibrium is singular; any of these would weaken the proposed tendon-mediated localization mechanism and reduce the value of searching routing variants.

interpretations.text: The frozen passive, unloaded local mechanism produced two converged qualified-local-minimum trials, requiring 14 and 70 optimizer iterations. The selected working point passed KKT, LICQ, second-order sufficiency, strict complementarity, contact-free, dual-nonnegative, length, and tendon-capacity checks. Its stationarity infinity norm was 2.131551974043997e-10 N·m, complementarity residual was 6.689144995757621e-16 N·m, and primal violation was 5.551115123125783e-17 m. The minimum slack margin was -5.551115123125783e-17 m and native soft-length excess was 5.551115123125783e-17 m; these tiny strict violations are retained even though the recorded tolerance-based qualification passed. All three tendons were active with positive equilibrium tensions, with maximum tension 1.7214417663040709 N; minimum reduced stiffness was 0.0920759180326094 N·m/rad. The initial preflight found zero native-enabled contacts and each tendon at a unilateral payout boundary, with path length 0.2540000000000002 m, payout 0.2540000000000001 m, and signed residual 1.1102230246251565e-16 m. Boundary activity alone does not measure tension or convert these channels into bilateral fixed-length constraints.

These observations support existence and local static stability qualification of at least one contact-free equilibrium branch in the declared ideal hard-unilateral, fixed-payout model at the standardized initial unloaded condition. They weaken an explanation based solely on numerical nonconvergence or failure to find any locally qualified equilibrium: both starts converged, and one working point satisfied the full recorded regularity and stability checks. However, the result does not establish global feasibility, structural necessity, robustness, or physical performance. Equilibrium, KKT regularity, and local stability are distinct from dynamic task behavior, and no parameter sensitivity, matched comparison, or structure direction was produced; therefore no causal mechanism change or beneficial design direction can be inferred.

Task success remains unresolved because dynamic validation was not evaluated and acceptance over the 8.0 s task horizon was unmeasured. The specifically missing evidence is complete dynamics, an independent replay, and the original task-acceptance evaluation. Until those results exist, the local time-0 static qualification cannot show whole-window compliance, dynamic improvement, repeatability, or failure. Collision clearance is also certified only for native-enabled pairs; excluded solid pairs remain unevaluated.
